content:
For a little while (a few weeks?) I've noticed that the automatically created mathlib PR testing branches for batteries PRs fail with the following error:

Run cd pr-branch
Removing old Mathlib build directories prior to cache fetch...
Attempting to fetch olean for Mathlib/Init.lean from cache...
uncaught exception: leantar not found in Lean sysroot. This toolchain may predate nightly-2026-03-09.

See for example batteries#1754.

Given the mention of 2026-03-09, I thought this might automatically resolve itself with time, but since it hasn't (yet), just wanted to bring this to someone's attention in case it needs to be fixed! :)
Oh, is this one of the issues mentioned in #batteries > batteries#1736 broke Mathlib (?) ?
I looked into it. The LEAN_SRC_PATH is not set properly but I couldn't figure out why nor how that would affect this step.
I notified @Kim Morrison but didn't hear back yet. (There's a lot of other recent issues that surely keep them busy.)
Ah, okay! By the way, what should the LEAN_SRC_PATH look like/what's wrong with it?
The last piece ends with /home/lean/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4--- and no version number.
Looking at the relevant script build_template.yml, I couldn't figure out why that would happen. If you or anyone has keener eyes, that would make me happy!

How strange! In the logs I'm looking at, though, I seem to see v4.29.0 after the --- in all the places I could find. Are these logs behaving differently from the ones you saw earlier, somehow? (Or am I just missing it, which is very possible? :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes:)
I see it in the logs for your batteries#1754 PR. You have to look closely at the failing cache step.

This step, right?

Run cd pr-branch
  cd pr-branch
  echo "Removing old Mathlib build directories prior to cache fetch..."
  rm -rf .lake/build/lib/lean/Mathlib

  # Fail quickly if the cache is completely cold, by checking for Mathlib.Init
  echo "Attempting to fetch olean for Mathlib/Init.lean from cache..."
  ../tools-branch/.lake/build/bin/cache get Mathlib/Init.lean
  shell: /usr/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail {0}
  env:
    LAKE_NO_CACHE: true
    CI_CHECKOUT_PATH: /home/lean/actions-runner/_work/mathlib4-nightly-testing/mathlib4-nightly-testing/ci-tools
    CI_SCRIPTS_DIR: /home/lean/actions-runner/_work/mathlib4-nightly-testing/mathlib4-nightly-testing/ci-tools/scripts
    TOOLCHAIN_DIR: /home/lean/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.29.0
    LEAN_SRC_PATH: .:/home/lean/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.29.0/src/lean/lake:.lake/packages/plausible:.lake/packages/LeanSearchClient:.lake/packages/importGraph:.lake/packages/proofwidgets:.lake/packages/aesop:.lake/packages/Qq:.lake/packages/batteries:.lake/packages/Cli
Removing old Mathlib build directories prior to cache fetch...
Attempting to fetch olean for Mathlib/Init.lean from cache...
uncaught exception: leantar not found in Lean sysroot. This toolchain may predate nightly-2026-03-09.
Error: Process completed with exit code 1.

(I just realized my use of "keener" is apparently just in Canadian English, it means something much darker in other variants. To me, it means "sharper and more motivated". Apologies for any confusion.)
That's how I interpret it too, as a U.S. English speaker! I've never heard another meaning, but I don't doubt there is one...

(Oh, apparently the noun specifically ("a keener"), meaning a person who is very eager, is exclusively Canadian English, and I indeed haven't heard that, but the comparative adjective with the meaning you gave seems nonspecific to a region :) )
Yes, it appears my eyes were not so keen in two different ways: I looked at the noun not the adjective and on another look, you're right that the path is correct. :upside_down:
Aha, I see, no problem! :)
In any case, this was a fun interaction that reminded me that I need to go to sleep very soon...
Same here! :) I'm glad you said something, I might have kept on investigating this :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes:
Goodnight! :moon: On the downside, I'm now more mystified about this issue. :/
(Kim is away for Easter)

Yes, I was hoping Kim would delegate to someone before leaving for Easter. Maybe @Bryan Gin-ge Chen or @Sebastian Ullrich would like to chime in, but this is Easter and Passover weekend so I wouldn't expect a response from anyone in particular until next week.

Thomas Murrills said:

Given the mention of 2026-03-09, I thought this might automatically resolve itself with time

It looks like you already were right on the money in your first message. This is an incompatiblity of mathlib4 master (which is what batteries testing branches are based on) with the mathlib4-nightly-testing CI (which is used for testing those branches) that should resolve itself with 30-rc1 (which I think is unblocked now)

Hmm, 4.30.0-rc1 was merged into mathlib with #37564 but there's a leantar not found in Lean sysroot in #37582 (which just merged master): https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/actions/runs/23993396427/job/69976975099?pr=37582
Ah, I've figured it out. Fix in #37653.
